turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Morning, come on in and have a seat. Bit grey out there, isn't it. How are you going?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh, um, I'm alright I s'pose. I don't know, doctor. They rang me.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): The clinic rang you, yeah. What did they say it was about?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): The blood thing. The warfarin one. They reckoned it was up and I should come in. That's why I'm here.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right, so we're looking at that INR today. Before I get into the number, tell me how you've been feeling in yourself.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Pretty ordinary. Err, I don't know. Not sick sick. Just off.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Off in what way?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): My daughter came to the locum with me, she does the talking. She told him I'd been dizzy and not eating, but I don't know, doctor, I wasn't dizzy.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): So you don't think you've been dizzy. What about the eating, have you changed what you eat?

[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Well, actually, yeah. She said the green stuff fights the Marevan, so I stopped the spinach and the broccoli. Haven't had any for, I don't know, a week? Maybe more. I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Okay, that's useful. We'll come back to the greens. Any bleeding you've noticed? Nosebleeds, blood in the wee, black bowel motions?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing like that. Um. Toothbrush was a bit pink yesterday. Or the day before. I don't know.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): A bit of pink on the brush. Gums a little raw?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): I s'pose. Not pouring out. My daughter reckons there's bruises on my arm but I can't see them. I don't know, doctor. I think she's seeing things.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Fair enough, we'll go with what you can see. Any fever, or waking up hot and sweaty?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. One night I felt warm, could've been the doona, the nights have been funny. I don't think I had a proper fever. Hard to say.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any cough, or getting puffed walking around the house?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Chest's been fine. No cough.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): And your weight, has that shifted at all, up or down?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Same belt hole for months. Hasn't shifted.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): That's alright. Now, you're on the Marevan for the atrial fibrillation, the little pink ones. Still taking those?

[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, the little pink ones, every night with the news. Except, um, I don't know if I missed one, my daughter says I skip them. I think I only forgot once, maybe. I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): The notes here say five milligrams, one pink tablet at night. Does that sound right?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): If you say so. I just take the pink one. I don't look at the number.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): And the other doctor started an antibiotic. Have you got the box?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Uh, in the bag. Those big white horse pills. She said they were for the bladder, the stinging.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): Let me see. Ciprofloxacin, five hundred milligrams, one twice a day. When did you start them?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. Tuesday? Or was it Monday. Last week sometime. I've still got some left.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Still taking them, morning and night?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah. I think I've been good with those. The bladder's settled, anyway.

[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Good. I'll just feel your pulse while we talk. It's irregular, which fits the fibrillation, and it's sitting around eighty four. Blood pressure's one thirty two over seventy eight.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Is that bad?

[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): No, that's a comfortable pressure, and the rate's fine. The rhythm's the old atrial fibrillation, nothing new there. The INR we did Tuesday has come back at four point two.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Is that the high one? I don't know what the number's meant to be.

[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): For the fibrillation we like it between two and three. Four point two is over, not dangerous on its own, but it's why the gums pinked up a bit. I reckon the cipro and dropping the greens have both pushed it up.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): So did I do the wrong thing with the broccoli? She was only trying to help. And that sipro stuff, I don't know.

[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): She meant well. Vitamin K in the leafy greens actually keeps the INR steady if you eat a similar amount most days. Stopping them suddenly lets the INR climb. You don't have to live on spinach, just don't swing from heaps to none.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm. I can have a bit of broccoli again then.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): Yes. A usual serve, not a bucket. Now the dose. I'd like you to drop from the five milligram pink tablet to the three milligram blue one, one at night, starting tonight.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): The little blue one instead. Every night?
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): Every night, same time, with the news if that's your habit. Finish the ciprofloxacin as the other doctor wrote it, don't stop it halfway.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay. I don't know how many days are left. The box might say.

[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): There's three days left on the label, so take them through to Sunday. For the INR, the nurse takes bloods next Thursday morning. Come in before you take the Marevan, you don't need to fast.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): Thursday morning, before the tablet. No brekkie rules.
[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): Exactly, eat as you like. I'll see you Thursday afternoon once that result's back, in a week.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): And if it's still up?
[SEG0047] person_1 (DOCTOR): If Thursday's number is still borderline, we do a full blood count as well, but I won't order that today.
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): Right.
[SEG0049] person_1 (DOCTOR): And if the gum bleeding doesn't settle, or you get black motions or a proper nosebleed, we organise a scan rather than waiting. Otherwise we leave it.
[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): I hope it just settles. I don't know, doctor, I get nervous with all this.
[SEG0051] person_1 (DOCTOR): That's understandable. Keep an eye on the gums, and ring us sooner if you're worried rather than sitting on it. Any questions before you go?
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I think I've got it. Blue tablet, Thursday morning, see you after. Thanks.

spec.situation: Older patient on warfarin for atrial fibrillation; INR result read aloud; antibiotic started elsewhere; green leafy diet changes; dose adjusted and recheck in a week.

traps.happens: In the plan the doctor books some tests or visits for a definite time ('the nurse takes bloods Thursday morning', 'I'll see you in two weeks') and makes others conditional ('if those are borderline we do the third test', 'if it does not settle, a scan').
traps.label_rule: Booked or arranged = status planned. Only the hedged ones are conditional. Never mark a booked test conditional or 'if needed'. Instructions for the booked test (fasting, time, medicine timing) belong to that test's action, not a separate invented plan item.

traps.happens: The doctor asks only two to four review-of-systems questions (for example fever, weight, cough). Several other body systems are never asked about. One of the asked questions gets a vague or mixed answer.
traps.label_rule: negative_findings / review_of_systems ONLY for items the doctor actually asked AND the patient answered, evidence = that question and answer. Never add review-of-systems entries for systems nobody asked about, and never cite an unrelated turn (for example a turn about tiredness) for a system review.

features: colloquial_drug_names: medicines referred to by colour, purpose or brand ('the water tablet', 'Crocin', 'my sugar tablets', 'the purple inhaler'); the name is recorded as said, the normalized name only if it is clear.
relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.

bad.reason: Mild gum bleeding and timing supported; certainty wrong because patient is tentative: 'I s'pose'.
bad.text: Gum bleeding (category=ENT, status=present, severity=mild, onset=yesterday or the day before, temporality=current, body_site=gums, reported_by=patient, certainty=certain)

bad.reason: Feeling warm one night is supported, but resolved status/temporality not stated.
bad.text: Feeling warm at night (category=constitutional, status=resolved, temporality=resolved, reported_by=patient, certainty=uncertain)

omissions.text: Patient denied being dizzy despite daughter having reported dizziness to the locum.
Patient reported possible bruises on the arm mentioned by daughter, but patient could not see them and was uncertain they were really present.
Patient did not think they had a proper fever despite one night of feeling warm; fever was specifically asked about and essentially denied/uncertain.
Warfarin adherence detail missing: patient takes it every night with the news but thinks they may have missed one dose/forgot once.
Ciprofloxacin start timing is recorded as uncertain, but it was specifically described as started Monday or Tuesday last week sometime and still being taken morning and night.
INR result value from Tuesday was 4.2, with target range 2 to 3 for atrial fibrillation.
